Twenty years I've been farming this land, ever since my father handed it over to me when I was 25. I've built it up to 58 mu now — that's a lot of ground for a household of four, so I have to think hard about what makes money and what I can actually manage. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and I talk to the seed dealer when he comes to the village, but mostly I do what worked last year and I watch the big farmers around me. My stevia is my main crop — I've got 25 mu of it — but I keep 20 mu in wheat and maize because that rotation is steady income and I need the grain, and I still have 13 mu of cotton because the price was decent last year and the dealer already gave me a good quote on seed.

For wheat, I plant Luyuan 502, it's an improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang has had good luck with on his big plot. After the maize comes off in October, I run the rotary tiller and broadcast about 35 jin of seed per mu. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — 100 kg of the 19-22-7 type — and then when the wheat turns green in March I topdress with another half-bag of compound and some urea. All together that's about 28 kg of nitrogen per mu. I irrigate four times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, and three times in spring when the heads are filling. The well can handle 58 mu but electricity costs money, so I don't waste water. For spraying, I do herbicide once before winter, insecticide twice in spring, and fungicide once if the spring is wet — four times total. I expect about 1000 kg per mu.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid the day after wheat harvest in June. No time to waste, the season is short. I don't till — just plant right into the wheat stubble with the no-till machine. Two bags of 27-6-7 compound fertilizer per mu, which is about 27 kg nitrogen. I irrigate twice because summer rains aren't reliable like they used to be. Herbicide once at planting and insecticide twice — three sprays total. I hire the machinery for planting and harvest; there's no way I could do 58 mu with just family labor, and hired labor is 150 yuan a day now. I expect around 1100 kg per mu.

Cotton is expensive to grow. I rotary till in April and plant Guoxinmian improved seed at about 3 jin per mu. The bollworms here are bad, so I spray 14 times total — mostly insecticide, plus herbicide once and fungicide once. I put down 100 kg of 28-0-8 compound at planting and another 100 kg of 19-22-7 when it flowers. That's about 47 kg nitrogen per mu. Three irrigations, timed when the bolls are setting. I expect about 550 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Stevia is where I make my real money. I rotary till and transplant Chengguang variety in mid-April, about 8000 plants per mu. Stevia drinks water — I irrigate six times through the season. I put 80 kg of 22-6-12 compound at planting and 120 kg of 15-15-15 after the first cutting. That's about 36 kg nitrogen, 23 kg phosphorus, 28 kg potassium per mu. I spray insecticide five times, fungicide twice, and herbicide once — eight times total. Last year I got 580 kg per mu of dry leaves; this year I'm hoping for 600. I hire four workers for transplanting week because 25 mu of hand-planting is too much for my family.

Everything is connected. If fertilizer prices go up again like they did two years ago, I might trim back a little on cotton topdressing, but I won't touch the stevia — that's my cash crop and I need it to pay for the hired labor and the electricity bill. Last year I bought a tractor-mounted sprayer for 8000 yuan, and it already saved me money on hired labor for spraying 58 mu. I'd rather put down a bit too much fertilizer than risk losing yield — a bad harvest is a disaster, but wasting some fertilizer is just money I might have spent for nothing.
